name: American English (General American)

ancestors.notes: Middle English descent via colonial English

notes: General American (GA) — reference accent for US media/education. RHOTIC: /r/ preserved in all positions. No TRAP-BATH split (bath words = /æ/). LOT-PALM merger: /ɑː/ for both. T-FLAPPING: /t/ → [ɾ] between vowels (butter, water, city). CAUGHT-COT merger common (thought = lot for most speakers). Source: Wells (1982) vol. 3, Ladefoged & Johnson (2011). FLAPPING: /t/ and /d/ → [ɾ] intervocalically in unstressed syllables (butter, ladder, city). RHOTIC: fully rhotic — /r/ preserved in all positions. GA GOAT is /oʊ/, not the RP /əʊ/ this spec's parent declares (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1.4). The RP coda-/r/ deletion this spec inherits is re-declared with no target phonemes (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1; Ladefoged & Johnson 2011) — the id-keyed way a dialect states it lacks a parent's process. SUFFIX PALATALIZATION, RHOTIC COLUMN: the three yod-coalescing suffixes this spec inherits end in a coda /r/ that GA keeps, so each is re-declared with the r-coloured schwa [ɚ] in place of the RP [ə]. ENDING "ture" is [tʃɚ] (nature, picture, feature) — the coalesced coronal plus GA r-coloured schwa (Wells 2008 LPD; Wells 1982 vol 3 §6.1). ENDING "sure" is [ʒɚ] (measure, closure, leisure) — the same, with the voiced coronal (Wells 2008 LPD; Wells 1982 vol 3 §6.1). ENDING "ssure" is [ʃɚ] (pressure, fissure) — the same after the voiceless ⟨ss⟩, which longest-match-wins picks over ⟨-sure⟩ (Wells 2008 LPD; Wells 1982 vol 3 §6.1).

location.notes: the geographic centre of the United States. General American is a media/education reference accent with NO regional home at all — this is the weakest point in the dataset and should be read as such. [Wikidata Q30 P625]

allophone_rules.notes: LOT-PALM merger: GA has no /ɒ/ - the RP LOT vowel merges with PALM as unrounded /ɑ/ (Wells 1982 vol.3 6.1.3).

General American is fully rhotic: /r/ is preserved in every position, so the RP coda-/r/ deletion this spec inherits does not apply (Wells 1982 vol.3 §6.1; Ladefoged & Johnson 2011). Declared with no target phonemes, the id-keyed way a dialect states it lacks a parent's process.
Same statement as EN_GB_NONRHOTIC_AR_PRECONS: this lect is rhotic, so it does not have the parent's coda-/r/ deletion.
